A1.justification: Both PDFs describe GSAlign and contain readable main text, equations, three figures, nine tables, and Appendix A.1–A.3. The complete material supports a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1.pdf reports original GSAlign experiments on CARGO, AG-ReID, and AG-ReID v2, component ablations, qualitative alignment examples, and inference-cost measurements.

after.justification: v2.pdf retains these original experiments and supplementary analyses, with revised GSAlign results on the two real-world datasets.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.4 retain the same backbone, LTPS transformations, training-only DAM, loss functions, and inference procedure. No algorithmic component is added or revised.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CARGO, AG-ReID, and AG-ReID v2 under the same matching scenarios in Tables 1–3. The appendix introduces no coverage differences.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the benchmark and supplementary comparisons. VDT is merely reordered in Table 3; the newly cited SD-ReID and LATex are not added to any reported evaluation.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 retains the same splits, metrics, backbone, preprocessing, optimizer, 120-epoch budget, and batch size. Revised protocol names in the AG-ReID v2 discussion match the existing Table 3 settings; they do not establish a changed evaluation design. No setting change accompanies the revised scores.

E4.justification: The component, control-point, insertion-depth, and DAM-variant analyses in Tables 4–7 are unchanged. Appendix A also retains identical alignment visualizations, deformation-constraint and original-TPS comparisons, and efficiency analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting procedure is added or revised.

E6.justification: All GSAlign scores in Tables 2–3 are revised downward under unchanged reported settings. AG-ReID A↔G Rank-1/mAP/mINP changes from 86.74/84.00/73.62 to 83.75/75.01/52.11; AG-ReID v2 A↔G Rank-1/mAP changes from 91.47/89.78 to 87.86/81.38. Rankings materially change: VDT now exceeds GSAlign on AG-ReID G↔A Rank-1 and mAP, and GSAlign loses its AG-ReID v2 A↔W mAP lead. CARGO and appendix results remain unchanged. The PDFs do not explain the numerical revisions.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, and Equations 1–14 are unchanged. Equation relocation across page boundaries introduces no new derivation or correction.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same geometric-and-semantic alignment contribution and state-of-the-art claims. The headline CARGO gains of 18.8 percentage points in mAP and 16.8 in Rank-1 remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 qualifies the real-world performance interpretation: AG-ReID G↔A changes from superior performance to competitive Rank-1/mAP, with new emphasis on hard-sample and long-tail retrieval through mINP. The AG-ReID v2 discussion acknowledges competitors' higher Rank-1 scores. General robustness interpretations and Appendix A.3 limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v1.pdf's abstract supplies a GitHub code link and availability statement; v2.pdf removes both without replacement. Implementation and timing details remain unchanged. This establishes reduced access information, not that the repository itself became unavailable.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds SD-ReID and LATex, briefly discussing diffusion-based representations and attribute-text knowledge. These two additional references modestly expand related-work coverage while retaining GSAlign's existing positioning.

P1.justification: The revision adds a short related-work passage, rewrites the real-world results discussion, and removes the abstract's code sentence. Section ordering and the remainder of the scientific exposition are substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: All figures and tables are retained. Table 3 moves the VDT row below SeCap, Tables 2–3 update best-score bolding, and text reflow shifts table placement and page breaks. The figures and appendix layout are unchanged.

improvement.justification: Added related-work context, corrected protocol descriptions, and more qualified performance discussion are useful. However, the substantial score replacements are unexplained, code-access information disappears, and Section 4.2 claims the highest mAP across all four AG-ReID v2 protocols despite Table 3 showing 83.98 versus the AG-ReIDv2 baseline's 84.85 on A↔W. These mixed effects, particularly the unresolved basis for the result revisions, prevent a reliable net-quality judgment.
